subject: FORGE FINALE -- state saved, stopped. 30/45 at session 49
body:
FORGE FINALE -- state saved, stopped at your word. 30/45, session 49 of 60.

Twelve sessions today, 24/45 to 30/45. Six criteria earned: the derivation field on every human log line, every line rewritten to clear its length rule, the multiplicity ledger, IC published as a curve instead of a point, purge and embargo on every split, and the uniqueness-weighted sample. C2.5 re-earned properly after its original pass was found resting on a checker that covered half its own rule.

Nothing is half-done. No EA source was touched in the last two sessions -- both were research-layer only. SLS(179) is the build on disk and deployed, 0 errors 0 warnings, byte-identical across all three locations, terminal never ran all day. No loop is armed.

Three things wait on you, all written up in the checkpoint:

The sample floor for reporting a win rate is now derived -- 1,309 trades, every input from your own constants. Every floor in the code is below it; the biggest is 500. I recommended printing the count and withholding the rate, the way the Python side already does. When you told me to stop waiting I started on it, then stopped again on a real hazard rather than pushing through: PrintFormat is variadic, so swapping a number for a string is not a compile error, it prints garbage at runtime. A hundred-and-eighteen-site rewrite that can fail silently needs a verifier built first. That is the honest reason it is not done.

Rate reports now all carry how many trades they came from -- 34 this morning, 118 of 118 tonight. The payoff half of that same criterion is at 24 of 118, which only became visible after I rewrote its check to be capable of failing.

And the holdout question: the out-of-sample window gets re-used on every retry, so 'used once' is not true today.

Where I was when you said stop: C1.4 finally has a call-site census -- 775 functions, 36 unreachable, 24 already documented as dead or held, 12 not. Five of those twelve are Living Edge helpers. Five at once reads like a subsystem that was built and never connected, and that is worth reading as one thing rather than twelve.

Everything else waits for Monday's open.
